headline: Rhode Island voter registration deadline arrives Sunday for November election
dek: Eligible Rhode Islanders have until 4 p.m. Sunday to register or update a voter record for the Nov. 3 general election, with mail-ballot and early-voting deadlines close behind.
body: Rhode Island’s deadline to register to vote or update a voter record for the Nov. 3 general election arrives Sunday, Oct. 4. Eligible residents must act by 4 p.m. to participate in the statewide election, according to the Rhode Island Department of State and the state’s 2026 election calendar. The deadline applies 30 days before Election Day and covers local, state and federal contests on the November ballot.

The state says residents can use the online voter-registration portal at [vote.ri.gov](https://vote.ri.gov/) or work with their local board of canvassers. The [Rhode Island Board of Elections registration guidance](https://elections.ri.gov/voter-resources) says an online registration or record update requires a Rhode Island driver’s license or state identification card. If an applicant does not have either document, the portal generates a form to print and mail to the local board. The Board of Elections also provides English and Spanish paper forms.

First-time applicants face an additional identification step under the federal Help America Vote Act. The Board of Elections says applicants should provide a valid Rhode Island driver’s-license or state-ID number, or the last four digits of a Social Security number if they have not been issued a Rhode Island license or ID. People who cannot provide those numbers may still register, but the state says they will need to present an accepted identification document before registering, before voting or at the polls. The agency lists documents such as a passport, student or employee ID, utility bill, bank statement, lease or government document.

For people who need to file a paper form Sunday, the Department of State published a list of drop-off sites operating around Rhode Island. Examples include the Public Safety Complex in Providence, the Blackstone Valley Visitors Center in Pawtucket, Cranston City Hall, the Newport City Hall municipal drop box and police or town facilities in communities including Barrington, Bristol, Cumberland, Middletown, Warwick and Woonsocket. Hours vary by location: some open in the morning, while others accept forms from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. The full list and local hours are in the [state’s deadline notice](https://www.sos.ri.gov/article?articleno=51498), and residents should check the listing before traveling.

The deadline comes as Rhode Island’s electorate moves from the September primary into a general election that includes congressional, statewide and local races. More than 695,000 eligible voters were registered in September, according to data cited by [Rhode Island Current](https://rhodeislandcurrent.com/2026/09/30/voter-registration-deadline-is-sunday-oct-4/) and maintained by the Department of State. About 52% were unaffiliated, 34% were Democrats and 14% were Republicans at that point, figures that describe the registration file rather than likely turnout or the outcome of any race.

Registration is the first of several fall deadlines. Registered voters who want to vote by mail must submit an application by 4 p.m. Tuesday, Oct. 13, according to the [state election calendar](https://vote.sos.ri.gov/Forms/Elections/Guides/2026ElecCal.pdf). The application is available online or on paper. In-person early voting begins Oct. 14 and continues through 4 p.m. Monday, Nov. 2, at locations designated by each city or town. The state says voters should confirm those locations and hours with their local board of canvassers or through the Department of State’s election website.

On Election Day, polls are scheduled to open at 7 a.m. and close at 8 p.m. across Rhode Island, except in New Shoreham, where polls open at 9 a.m. Anyone in line at closing time may still vote, according to the official calendar. Residents can check their registration status and polling place at [vote.sos.ri.gov](https://vote.sos.ri.gov/) before heading to a registration site or making a voting plan. The state’s online resources remain the best source for any change to a deadline, address or local procedure.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Rhode Island voter registration deadline is Oct. 4, 2026
seoDescription: Rhode Island voters have until 4 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, to register for the Nov. 3, 2026 general election.
